Alex — quick technical notes on rate caps and routing so expectations match what Ops will provision:

- "RPS account-level" vs "per-route": Account-level RPS is enforced early in the proxy. If you increase account-level RPS to 250 but leave heavy routes unthrottled, a single route can consume most of the capacity. I recommend per-route quotas such as:
  - Search-indexing: 300 RPS (best-effort)
  - User-facing chat/recommendations: 400 RPS (higher priority)
  - Background batch scoring: 50 RPS (low priority)

- Cache/prefixing: Add a small prefix cache on recommendation calls; that will reduce token usage significantly for repeated queries. We've seen 20-30% token reduction in similar e-commerce workloads.

- Burst windows: the 48-hour 1,000 RPS burst will require a temporary autoscaling policy. We'll pre-allocate capacity but keep it gated behind a toggle so Ops can flip it on for your test window.

Happy to run a short runbook exercise with your SREs if you want to validate behavior under the burst.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: rate_limit_proposal.xlsx (XLSX)
